decisions.question: Does stating the replay tool's landing phases, its command-line semantics and the 'first producing phase' wording amend ADR-001 in place, or does it need a superseding ADR?

options.label: amend in place
options.consequence: Item numbers, status, date and every Governed by link stay; a fourth dated entry under ## Amendments lists what moved.

options.label: supersede with ADR-004
options.consequence: A new file restating ADR-001 with the additions; ADR-001 becomes superseded and all eighteen Governed by links and every 'ADR-001 item N' citation in specs and contracts move, with no change to what binds.

decisions.why: No decision changes: every rule written down was taken in nidana.model D1 or D2 (or nidana.model.7's scope) and is what the reconciled gates already assume. hsdd-adr reserves supersession for a later ADR that replaces this one; the two earlier in-place amendments set the precedent for clarifications of this kind, and nidana.model D2 itself calls these 'a candidate clarification at its next touch'.

decisions.question: Item 9 'written in its first phase': state the four landing phases in the ADR, or only point at nidana.model D1 and the conventions' replay-tool list?

options.label: state the phases, citing D1
options.consequence: A third copy of the list (D1, conventions, ADR), but the one hsdd-config injects into every phase context, including phases of other nodes that run a set.

options.label: point at D1 and the conventions
options.consequence: One fewer copy to drift, but a consuming node's phase context, which never carries nidana.model's D{n}, would read only a pointer.

decisions.why: hsdd-config injects an ADR's Decision into every governed phase's context, while a node-local D{n} reaches only that node's phases, so stating the phases is what makes a lint or codegen phase see its edge on nidana.model.7. Drift risk is low because every contract's phase_ids are final (S42). Close call: had the plans still been provisional, the pointer would have been the better choice.

decisions.question: Where do the command-line semantics go: new sub-bullets of item 9, or a new item 13?

options.label: item 9 sub-bullets
options.consequence: Item 9 keeps owning the command, sets, restriction and runners; every existing 'ADR-001 item 9' citation (PENDING, --guarantee, runners) now lands on the full rule.

options.label: new item 13
options.consequence: Item 9 untouched apart from the landing phases, but the restriction and PENDING rules would be split across two items and the existing citations would point at half of each.

decisions.why: Contracts and plans cite item 9 for PENDING, --guarantee and the runners (bus-api@v1, bus-testing@v1, navigation-api@v1, flutter-binding@v1 Validation; nidana.runtime replay schedule), so completing item 9 keeps those citations exact and moves no item number.

decisions.question: With the suite-keyed restriction, does item 9 also state that a {slug}/G{n} may name a slug the command does not replay?

options.label: state it
options.consequence: nidana.runtime.12's and .13's gates, which pass topology-dsl/G18 to G29 to a bus-api replay, are legal by the ADR's text.

options.label: leave it implicit
options.consequence: A tool that treats an id of an unreplayed slug as D2's 'unknown slug' usage error would fail those two gates with exit 64.

decisions.why: It is what those gates already assume, and the suite-keying rule S31 asked for has no use without it, since a cross-slug binding's cases can only be named by a qualified id of a slug other than the replayed one. No gate command changes.

decisions.question: Does the empty-selection rule (no admitted case: not run, counts as passing) cover bindings only, as S31 stated it, or bindings, file replays and recorded invocations alike?

options.label: bindings, file replays and recorded invocations
options.consequence: One rule covers nidana.navigation.2 to .5 and nidana.flutter.2 to .6 (bindings) and nidana.tooling.lint.1 to .3 (a cli selection with no case), which today read it from nidana.model D2 items 1 and 4.

options.label: bindings only
options.consequence: The file and cli case follows from 'runs only when every id is in the restriction' by inference, as lint D3 item 2 reads it, with the ADR silent.

decisions.chosen: bindings, file replays and recorded invocations
decisions.why: Every gate that admits no case relies on the same outcome; for file and cli it is already implied, so stating it once costs nothing and removes the inference. The binding half is the one that matters at run time, since dart test exits 79 on a filter that admits nothing.

decisions.question: Does item 9 state the one 'pub get --enforce-lockfile' before the file or cli set and its failure as an environment error (S21), which only nidana.model.7's scope and D2 item 1 hold today?

options.label: state it
options.consequence: A stale resolution becomes exit 2 by the ADR, never a case failing with dart run's exit 255 from a files/ directory.

options.label: leave it to nidana.model.7
options.consequence: The ADR stays silent; the rule binds only through nidana.model's plan, which nidana.tooling's phase contexts never carry.

decisions.why: nidana.tooling.codegen's and nidana.tooling.lint's gates rely on recorded invocations never reporting a resolution problem as the case's exit code; the rule is already planned (nidana.model.7 scope (4)), so writing it down changes no gate.

decisions.question: How does item 10 (and Context bullet 1) define 'first producing phase': the first phase produced_by names, or the first phase of the producing leaf-parent that produced_by names?

options.label: first phase of its producing leaf-parent in produced_by
options.consequence: Exact for one-producer contracts and gives each producer of nidana-checks@v1 its own first producing phase.

options.label: first phase produced_by names
options.consequence: Shorter, but nidana-checks@v1's produced_by lists nidana.tooling.lint.1 first while nidana.tooling.codegen's first producing phase is nidana.tooling.codegen.7.

decisions.chosen: first phase of its producing leaf-parent in produced_by
decisions.why: produced_by lists are in phase order per leaf-parent, but a contract with two producers concatenates them, so 'the first listed' misreads it. What item 10 requires of a gate is unchanged.

decisions.question: Item 11 'once the producer's first phase has merged': replace with 'first producing phase', or with the phase the contract's Delivery paragraph names for a consumer's edge?

options.label: the Delivery paragraph's phase
options.consequence: Matches the conventions' reading rule and every Delivery paragraph: topology-dsl@v1's consumers wait on nidana.model.5.

options.label: first producing phase
options.consequence: Uniform wording with item 10, but wrong for topology-dsl@v1, whose first producing phase is nidana.model.4 while its consumers must wait on nidana.model.5 for the shared main library to complete.

decisions.why: The conventions (Phase design, line 133) already read 'the producer's first phase' this way, and topology-dsl@v1's Delivery paragraph shows the two phases differ. Item 10 keeps 'first producing phase' because it is about where declarations land, item 11 about when a consumer may start.

decisions.question: The Consequences bullet 'Replaying a contract before its producer's first phase has merged fails with PENDING': re-key it to the first producing phase, or to the producing package's absence?

options.label: the producing package's absence
options.consequence: True for every contract: PENDING is about package_config, and a gate placed before the package exists fails, never passes.

options.label: the first producing phase
options.consequence: False for topology-dsl@v1 and topology-ir@v1: nidana_dart_contracts exists from nidana.model.3, so a replay between nidana.model.3 and .4 fails on missing declarations, not with PENDING.

decisions.why: The literal swap would make the bullet wrong for two contracts that share a package created by another contract's first producing phase. No gate replays a contract in that window, since each contract's sets beyond structure and schema first run at its own first producing phase.

decisions.question: Item 9 says which flutter a Flutter binding runs (the SDK of the running dart), and nidana.model.7 says a file command's leading 'fvm dart' runs as the running dart, but nothing says which dart a recorded invocation whose args first line is 'dart' runs (the eight analyze-* cases of nidana-checks@v1). State it in this amendment?

options.label: leave the ADR silent
options.consequence: No new rule in a step that adds none; under 'fvm dart run' the child's PATH begins with the pinned SDK, so 'dart' by name is the pinned one.

options.label: state it
options.consequence: Uniform with the binding rule, but a rule neither D2 nor any plan has taken, written in a pass that only records taken decisions.

decisions.why: The experiment shows fvm prepends the pinned SDK's bin to PATH for the tool's children, even with every other dart removed from PATH, so every gate (which runs the tool through fvm dart) gets the pinned SDK either way. Decided after the experiment ran; the timestamp was taken when recording. Signal that would change it: a gate or CI job that runs the tool without fvm beside another Dart SDK on PATH.

experiments.question: Under 'fvm dart run', which dart does a child process started by the name 'dart' get, compared with the SDK of the running dart?
experiments.finding: Platform.resolvedExecutable is the pinned SDK (3.47.7, Dart 3.13.5), and fvm puts /Users/mohamad.purbo/fvm/versions/3.47.7/bin first on the child's PATH, so 'dart' by name resolves to the pinned SDK, also with PATH stripped of every other dart. No ADR change needed for the cli set's 'dart' first line while gates run the tool through fvm.

Item 9: 'written in its first phase' replaced by the four landing phases (structure at nidana.model.1; surface, reject, schema, fixture.dart and PENDING detection at nidana.model.2; behavior at nidana.model.6; file and cli at nidana.model.7) and the edge another node's phase takes on the phase landing a set it runs; structure runs whether --set names it or not, and --set never adds a set a slug lacks; --guarantee takes {slug}/G{n} and bare G{n}, a bare id belongs to the one slug named and is a usage error with several, a {slug}/G{n} may name an unreplayed slug; a binding's restriction is keyed by the slug whose conformance library it imports; file replays and recorded invocations run only when every declared id is admitted, and a slug with no id of its own runs none; a binding, file replay or recorded invocation with no admitted case is not run and passes, and no runner gets a filter that admits nothing (dart test exits 79); one pub get --enforce-lockfile before the file or cli set; PENDING for every surface, reject or behavior library, file replay or recorded invocation naming an absent package; exit codes 0, 1, 2, 64 replace 'non-zero on any failure'.

What moved, continued.
